verdicts.evidence: Commit a5460e4ef adds txSetupStatus and WcTxSetupIndicator in TestCtrls.e2e.tsx, which render e2e-wc-tx-setup-ready/-failed markers. Commit 751b2079e makes the tx flows wait on the ready marker. The round-2 review confirms the fix.

Commit 3a5f8b6e0 adds a comment in WcResponseIndicator.tsx: "Flows drive one tx at a time; the last-key read relies on that, not on key order". This is the comment the bot suggested, tying the logic to the flow contract.

proposeFetchMock.ts now has a JSDoc note ("Install-once per JS runtime: the wrapper binds the underlying fetch at install time, so anything swapping global.fetch must do so before installing"). That is the remedy the bot proposed for this concern.
The install-once contract is now documented in the module JSDoc of proposeFetchMock.ts (lines 1-9). The round-2 review marks it ✅.
In WcResponseIndicator.tsx the useEffect now takes the deps array [outstanding], and Object.keys moved inside the effect (commit 3a5f8b6e0).

Commit 751b2079e adds shared wcTxUiTimeout/wcTxNetworkTimeout to e2e/utils/scripts/defaults.js. The flows (e.g. tx-send-happy.yml) now use ${output.defaults.wcTx*Timeout} instead of hard-coded values.

The flagged assertion at tx-send-happy.yml:48 now uses '.*-0\.001.*' (the signed amount), and the round-2 review marks it addressed. The pending-list assertion at line 94 still uses the loose pattern.

jitteredValue in walletConnectDappsSetup.ts still uses Date.now() + ++jitterSeq; only its comments were reworded. No human replied; the only reaction is the bot's own round-2 note calling it acceptable.
